tagline: West from Petersburg, nine days behind a retreating army.
intro: The driving tour follows the Army of Northern Virginia through its last days, April 1 to 9, 1865, from Petersburg to Appomattox Court House. The line drawn here keeps to one road west out of Petersburg, through Sutherland and Ford, Nottoway and Burkeville, past the turn for Sailor's Creek near Rice, then on through Prospect and Pamplin to Appomattox. The full tour strays off it to Amelia Court House, Sailor's Creek, Cumberland Church and High Bridge.
Lee was making for supplies at Farmville. The Union army kept pace, and the country of creeks and high bluffs did his long wagon trains no favors.

moments.title: Sailor's Creek Battlefield
moments.text: On April 6, 1865, Lee lost about 7,700 men and eight generals here, and watching from a bluff he asked whether the army had dissolved.

moments.title: High Bridge
moments.text: Confederates set the railroad bridge afire on April 7, Union engineers cut the burning span away, and after the surrender Lee told the men who had burned it to go home and rebuild it.

moments.title: Appomattox Court House
moments.text: The village where Lee surrendered on April 9 had already begun to fade, after the railroad passed it by for Appomattox Depot in 1854.
